## What this file is, and who reads it

`logs/known-failure-modes.md` is the page `build-agent` and `pipeline-agent` read at activation
step 0, so it is capped: at most 20 lessons per section, and at most 6 finding ids per
table cell. **This file is where everything those two limits exclude actually lives.**

Nobody loads it on activation. Read it when the digest points you here — a capped-section note, or
a `(+N earlier — see appendix)` in a table cell — or when you want the full history of one class.

A capped lesson is not a less important lesson. The cap keeps the digest affordable to read on
every dispatch; it is not a judgement that what it hides is settled.

## Before you execute a build config — capped lessons

*70 lesson(s) the digest does not render, in the same order it ranked them.*

- `gitleaks detect` scans commit HISTORY by default. Without --no-git it can report PASS over none of the files the build actually packages.  
  <sub>IMP-0002 · `gate-cannot-fail`</sub>
- Before packaging, if secret-scan or gate-input-tracking fails on a file under provisioning/certs/ or provisioning/deploymentSettings/ that `git check-ignore -v` confirms is gitignored, check whether it is a known Pester fixture (BuildGates.Tests.ps1's gitleaks-scope-probe.pem; DataverseScripts.Tests.ps1's acc-settings.json, IMP-0410) left behind by an interrupted local test run before assuming it is a real credential or a config defect — read the file/mtime, confirm the fixture marker text ('NOT-A-REAL-KEY-scope-probe'), delete it with a standalone Bash call (a combined cd+rm chain was refused by the Auto Mode classifier here; a standalone absolute-path rm was not), and re-run the gate. The durable fix is widening every glob over these two directories to route through scripts/lib/tracked_paths.py's tracked_glob(), not re-diagnosing this by hand every time a Pester run is interrupted.  
  <sub>IMP-0591 · `gate-scope-mismatch`</sub>
- A blocked_on note's re-test command is untested content and can produce a FALSE NEGATIVE that confirms the note. Before trusting a `pac admin list --name <x>` / draft_command style re-test, grep the identifier it passes against the rest of the config: this file named the DEV environment 'Revitalise Grant Automation (DEV)' in the one command meant to check for it and REV-GrantApplications-DEV in eight other places, so the check could only ever report the environment missing. Two corollaries, both seen in the same sitting: a note's blocker may already be SATISFIED by values the repository has been tracking for weeks (the DEV environment id and url were in four settings files), and a note's blocker may be DISPROVED rather than expired (ensure-auditing.ps1 already was the C-TECH-064 read-back the step said it was awaiting, and was already wired executably three times over). Re-test means run the thing, having first checked that the thing you are about to run asks the right question.  
  <sub>IMP-0587 · `gate-cannot-fail`</sub>
- Before obeying verify-improvement-log.py's citation-stamp WARNING, open the review document it names and check WHERE the id appears: an id quoted as a value -- 'the max read IMP-nnnn at that moment', a range endpoint, a count -- is not a processing claim, and stamping the entry with that review writes a false disposition that makes it read `awaiting-approval` against a document whose keyword resolves nothing. Stamp only where the review actually processed the finding. The durable fix is to decide substantiveness POSITIVELY (a CLUSTER block, a Cites: line, a change-table row) rather than by subtracting known non-scope positions, which the function's own docstring already argues for.  
  <sub>IMP-0495 · `gate-fires-on-nothing`</sub>
- Reproducing CI's verdict by copying the tree and excluding untracked paths BY NAME reproduces your own list, not git's — the paths you did not think of stay in. For forms-and-views-reachable the real commit-scoped figure is 10 warnings across 11 entities, not the 14 recorded in IMP-0437 and the Dev Summary's section 11: that 14 kept the two untracked round-statistics entity directories, worth 4 warnings, while excluding the two untracked rev_roundfinance folders. Use `python3 scripts/verify-forms-and-views-reachable.py --committed-only <root>` and read the scope line, never an rsync copy.  
  <sub>IMP-0445 · `gate-scope-mismatch`</sub>
- A `ts` in logs/improvement-log.jsonl is NOT comparable across sessions: stamps ~4h apart were written the same afternoon, and one entry in a hundred carries a UTC offset while the rest carry none. When you close an entry needing `reobserved`, stamp it on the SAME clock as the entry's own `ts` and state the wall-clock reading in `reobserved.result` - do not pick a number that merely passes the gate, and do not rewrite another session's ts. The mechanical fix, if this recurs, is to require an ISO-8601 offset on `ts` for new entries (forward-bound, like the evidence_grep needle in IMP-0181) so the ordering the gate asserts is about events rather than about clocks.  
  <sub>IMP-0432 · `gate-scope-mismatch`</sub>
- verify-tad-coverage.py scans EVERY *.md under docs/architecture for bolded deliverable-now claims naming rev_* columns, not only the file given to --tad - read a gate's argparse defaults before concluding that a delta document is out of its scope.  
  <sub>IMP-0382 · `gate-scope-mismatch`</sub>
- When a review's fix is 'move the rule into one place and have the callers use it', the deliverable is TWO things: the shared implementation, and a check that enumerates the callers FROM SOURCE. If the second is a list of names in a shell script, the fix has a shelf life measured in days — IMP-0093 to IMP-0232 was three. Ask of every proposed gate: what is the SET this applies to, and is that set read or typed? A typed set needs a second gate asserting it is complete, at which point reading it was cheaper.  
  <sub>IMP-0241 · `gate-cannot-fail`</sub>
- A Code App's power.config.json is deployable config, not just a local manifest: it pins environmentId and appId to one environment and the pipeline has no step that retargets either. Before promoting a code app beyond DEV, decide explicitly whether these two keys are a C-TECH-047 breach (then template them per environment) or a sanctioned exception (then record it in contract/known-exceptions.json with an owner and an expiry) -- and note that `pa app push -e/--environment-id` and `pa app init -e` both take the environment on the command line, which is the mechanism that makes per-environment retargeting possible without editing the file.  
  <sub>IMP-0205 · `gate-cannot-fail`</sub>
- A path-kind evidence rule only proves a directory or file exists, never that a specific named deliverable inside it is present. When a task's own description names multiple items (e.g. three security roles: admin, finance, trustee), give it a rule that checks each by name and reports partial when any are absent, instead of accepting the directory's mere existence as complete.  
  <sub>IMP-0152 · `gate-cannot-fail`</sub>
- When a new scripts/verify-*.py (or any --check-capable) script is added, wire it into every build config it applies to (or add it to SUITE_GATE_EXEMPT with a reason) in the SAME change — verify-build-config.py's suite-gate-is-not-a-step check exists for exactly this and does not run itself.  
  <sub>IMP-0568 · `gate-cannot-fail`</sub>
- scripts/verify-review-document.py's STALE-HEADER check only sees the literal word AWAITING; a header saying DRAFT, PARKED, PENDING or NOT APPLIED above an Applied section passes clean. Until it uses an allowlist, do not treat its OK line as evidence your status header is consistent - read the header against the body yourself before closing a review. And when you rewrite a header with sed or a python string replace, assert the replacement actually matched: a no-match is silent and leaves the stale text in place.  
  <sub>IMP-0558 · `gate-fires-on-nothing`</sub>
- Naming the findings a review deliberately excluded is REQUIRED by activation step 2 and currently trips 4 stamp warnings per excluded id. Do not respond by omitting the ids - the silent cap is the worse defect. Expect the warnings, say in the gate output that they are this shape, and let the declared-field remedy land: an 'excluded_by' field mirroring 'appended_by', which is the same altitude the appended_by decision was taken at.  
  <sub>IMP-0557 · `gate-fires-on-nothing`</sub>
- This is IMP-0007's pattern ('the `! grep ... && echo` gate pattern turns EVERY grep failure -- including exit 1 no-match -- into a PASS') committed by an agent that had read that exact line in logs/known-failure-modes.md at activation, which is evidence that knowing the pattern does not prevent it when the shell is being used as a notepad rather than as a gate. When batching several measurements into one shell invocation, separate them with `;` not `&&`, and echo a labelled line per measurement so a missing label is visible as a gap. A count you EXPECTED to be zero, arriving as an absence, is the specific shape to distrust. The durable half is agents/improvement-agent.md step 8: re-run every measurement a draft asserts, unchained, before applying it.  
  <sub>IMP-0542 · `gate-cannot-fail`</sub>
- Before parking a review at its gate, SIMULATE the disposition against scripts/verify-improvement-log.py --check on a scratch copy of the log and confirm the triggers the review exists to clear actually clear. 'NEW plus revisit_when' does NOT discharge the blocker rung - only APPLIED/REJECTED, or NEW plus an explicit deferred_reason, does. A V5 entry that honestly cannot be closed therefore needs a deferred_reason recording that decision, not merely a revisit_when; the gate's own message names deferred_reason as the second legitimate discharge.  
  <sub>IMP-0516 · `gate-scope-mismatch`</sub>
- Before asking the reviewer (or dispatching any agent) to perform a V4 action — open a form, judge a rendered screen, save/re-register a flow trigger — confirm the specific component is actually live in the target environment first. If it is not yet deployed, defer the ask until after Pipeline's own deploy step, the same way IMP-0503 deferred C-TECH-053's flow-trigger check.  
  <sub>IMP-0505 · `gate-scope-mismatch`</sub>
- Before failing a Test Report on a V4-class constraint (a human-in-designer save, a live trigger confirmation), confirm whether the required evidence could exist at Test time at all for the artifact under test, or whether it structurally can only be produced by the Pipeline V4 step that runs after Test's own gate. If the latter, defer that specific check to Pipeline's own V4 step and cite it as deferred-to-pipeline in the Test Report, rather than FAIL.  
  <sub>IMP-0503 · `gate-scope-mismatch`</sub>
- A review that adds a verify-*.py MUST record the wiring decision in its own change table — wired HARD, wired SOFT via --warn-only, or added to verify-build-config.py's SUITE_GATE_EXEMPT with a reason. There is no fourth option: an unwired verify-*.py turns the build config preflight red, so 'ship the script and wire it later' is not a state this repository has. Concretely, the SOFT mechanism is a command ending --warn-only, because scripts/ci/run-config-steps.sh halts on the first non-zero exit and has no per-step record-but-continue mode.  
  <sub>IMP-0491 · `gate-cannot-fail`</sub>
- Never continue a PowerShell string concatenation across a line break inside a cmdlet parameter argument - the + binds to that argument and re-parses the statement, so a piped subject arrives as $null and the assertion reports on nothing. This is IMP-0142's property, not its cmdlet: it holds for Should -Because exactly as it holds for Write-Output -f. Build the whole string inside one set of parens first, or keep it on one line.  
  <sub>IMP-0476 · `two-invocation-paths-disagree`</sub>
- In Pester, use `Should -Match ([regex]::Escape(...))` and never `-BeLike` when the needle contains a flow expression - item()?['rev_x'] carries [ ] and -BeLike reads those as a character class. -BeLike fails loudly and -Not -BeLike passes vacuously, so the dangerous half is the negative assertion: an absence test whose needle can never match is a test that cannot fail.  
  <sub>IMP-0475 · `gate-cannot-fail`</sub>
- Before writing a flow expression an approved ADR specifies, run the flow's OWN build gates against a scratch copy of the intended shape rather than trusting the ADR's list of gate interactions - an ADR that names one gate has usually checked one gate. And when a gate must be widened for an approved design, widen it with an ANCHORED TEMPLATE over the whole expression, never by adding a function name to an allow-list: adding xpath/join/xml to verify-flow-trigger-body-isolation.py's reducing set would have exempted join(body('List_applications_in_round'), ','), which serialises rows into a column a trustee reads. The safety argument that licenses the template is one sentence - an XPath sum() returns a NUMBER and a number cannot carry a row - and it holds whatever the feeding Select projects.  
  <sub>IMP-0472 · `gate-scope-mismatch`</sub>
- THIRD instance of this check over-firing on an honest review (after IMP-0196's heading and improvement review 19's paragraph rule). Two things a review author needs today: SCOPE_DISCLAIMER matches 'left unprocessed' and NOT 'left unread', and a disclaimer governs ONE PARAGRAPH — so every paragraph that names a deferred finding id needs its own 'not processed in this review' clause, even one whose purpose is only context. And the general shape: a gate that decides INTENT by matching a phrase list will keep meeting phrasings the list lacks, and each instance-level widening guarantees the next one. Assert on a VALUE instead — the review's own explicit disposition per finding — rather than on the prose around the id.  
  <sub>IMP-0471 · `gate-fires-on-nothing`</sub>
- Measure the quantity a new gate depends on BEFORE writing the gate, with a throwaway probe, so the gate's first run has a number to be wrong against. Two independent implementations of the same extraction reported 0 against a flow containing 8, and both exited 0 — the only reason either was caught is that 8 had already been measured. Two concrete traps for Power Automate definitions: (1) a recursive walk over `actions` misses an action nested in a Scope inside a condition, and misses it silently; (2) when attributing a match to an enclosing JSON block by brace matching, take the NARROWEST enclosing block — the outermost one is `properties` and always matches, which turns a per-action classification into a whole-file one. Prefer classifying by a VALUE the block itself carries (here: the action composes "status":"ok") over classifying by the action's NAME — the name regex would have treated three of this flow's four non-ok documents as the OK one.  
  <sub>IMP-0458 · `gate-cannot-fail`</sub>
- contract/tad-deferrals.json's `deferrals` array holds ABSENT TAD 3.1 COLUMNS ONLY - every entry is matched against one, and an entry matching none FAILS the HARD tad-coverage gate as a dead promise. Do not put a response-document field, a requirement, or any other non-column gap in it, however directly a defect report names the file: run `python3 scripts/verify-tad-coverage.py --deferrals <your copy>` on a scratch copy BEFORE editing the tracked file. Non-column gaps go in the `undelivered_requirements` key added 2026-08-28, and that key is read by no gate - it is a dated written record, not a control, so it only works while a corrected Appendix A row and a 11 risk row point at it.  
  <sub>IMP-0455 · `gate-scope-mismatch`</sub>
- IMP-0410's class cuts BOTH ways: a gitignored file can turn a gate red, and an UNTRACKED file can turn one quiet. verify-forms-and-views-reachable.py globs directories without asking git, so untracked FormXml/SavedQueries content suppresses warnings locally that CI still emits — measured 12 warnings here versus 14 on a clean tree, over rev_roundfinance. Before transcribing any gate's warning COUNT into a document, run `git status --porcelain` over the paths that gate reads; and to reproduce CI's verdict cheaply, rsync the solution tree excluding untracked paths and re-run there rather than deleting another session's in-flight work.  
  <sub>IMP-0437 · `gate-scope-mismatch`</sub>
  <br><sub>**⚠ CORRECTED by `IMP-0445`** — a later finding contradicts this lesson. Read both before acting on it; the marker does not decide which is right.</sub>
- design-doc-claims reporting OK does NOT mean a corrected fact is consistent - it means no line in docs/architecture or docs/plans matched its two patterns. When you correct a schema fact in a design document, grep the WHOLE repository for the fact in its paraphrased forms too, source comments included: `grep -rn 'ethnic' src/ docs/` found two survivors after the gate went green, one of them a TSX comment citing the very sections just corrected. A code comment that cites a document section by number is a forward reference that rots silently when that section is rewritten, and no gate in this repository reads code comments for schema claims.  
  <sub>IMP-0430 · `gate-scope-mismatch`</sub>
  <br><sub>**⚠ CORRECTED by `IMP-0442`** — a later finding contradicts this lesson. Read both before acting on it; the marker does not decide which is right.</sub>
- verify-design-doc-claims.py cannot tell a retraction from an assertion, so writing an erratum that corrects a false-absence claim will turn the gate RED on the erratum's own prose. Two workarounds that do NOT weaken it: state the correction source-first ('`rev_x` exists; this document twice asserted the opposite') so no column name sits within 40 characters before an absence phrase, and keep the OLD contrast figure out of any markdown TABLE ROW - check (b) reads table rows only and prose is out of scope by design, so the retracted figure belongs in the paragraph, while the CORRECT figure stays in the row where it recomputes and counts as verified. Do NOT edit the script to clear your own gate: its 19-check --selftest is the thing protecting the two real defect shapes, and narrowing it is improvement-agent's call.  
  <sub>IMP-0428 · `gate-fires-on-nothing`</sub>
  <br><sub>**⚠ CONTESTED by `IMP-0535`** — a later finding disputes a claim in this lesson and NEITHER has been re-tested. Read that entry before relying on this one; it carries the form that is safe under either answer.</sub>
- A gate that counts rows 'of section N' must be scoped to section N's body, not to the file: an improvement review document carries a Type column in BOTH section 3 (proposed) and section 10 (applied), so a file-wide count doubles every figure. More generally, and this is the transferable half: when APPLYING a review, a gate measured during the DRAFT was measured against a tree that the application itself then changes -- the review document grows a section 10, statuses move, scripts appear. Re-run every gate the review touches AFTER the last edit, not only before the first. Review 33 measured 0 findings, applied its changes, and the same check then measured 5 against the same document.  
  <sub>IMP-0427 · `gate-scope-mismatch`</sub>
- verify-tad-coverage.py reads docs/architecture ONLY, because --design-docs defaults there and no caller overrides it -- the three documents under docs/plans/ are read by no gate at all for their deliverable-now claims. improvement review 33's change 7 (verify-design-doc-claims.py) covers BOTH directories deliberately for this reason, but it checks two claim types, not this one. When a gate takes a path argument with a default, check what else now lives where the default does not point.  
  <sub>IMP-0425 · `gate-scope-mismatch`</sub>
  <br><sub>**⚠ CORRECTED by `IMP-0440`** — a later finding contradicts this lesson. Read both before acting on it; the marker does not decide which is right.</sub>
- proposed_change in logs/improvement-log.jsonl is EITHER an object with type/target/summary OR a bare string -- the structural schema accepts both, and roughly one entry in two hundred uses the string. Any code reading its sub-fields must guard with isinstance(x, dict) rather than the `or {}` idiom, which defends against None and not against a string. More generally: a gate whose failure mode is an uncaught exception reports nothing while still exiting 0, so a wrapper checking only the exit status reads the crash as a pass -- when a check raises, that is a gate-cannot-fail finding, not a bad input.  
  <sub>IMP-0424 · `gate-cannot-fail`</sub>
- A count assertion must take its count from the SUBJECT, never from a list the test writes out itself - `Object.keys(map).length` against a literal, not a loop over a hand-written array of names. A test that enumerates its own subjects can only detect a removal and is structurally blind to an addition, so it goes on passing while the thing it guards grows. Sixth recorded instance of the count-coupling class and the FIRST that fails by staying green: when you find one of these, check which direction it can actually detect.  
  <sub>IMP-0416 · `hand-maintained-count-drifts-from-source`</sub>
- To run ONE vitest file in this repo, use 'npm --prefix src/code-apps/trustee-review-portal run test -- <path>', never 'npm --prefix <app> exec -- vitest run <path>': the exec form does not discover the app's vitest.config.ts, so its server.deps.inline entries vanish and Fluent/tabster fails to load as ESM. A green or red result from an invocation path the build never uses is evidence about neither the code nor the build -- IMP-0026's rule (verify through the path CI actually uses) applied to a single-file run.  
  <sub>IMP-0394 · `two-invocation-paths-disagree`</sub>
- A disk-read stylesheet test proves what a file SAYS, never that anything loads it — so it cannot see a deleted import, which is the exact failure the technique is usually adopted to guard. When a global stylesheet is added to this app, assert the side-effect import in main.tsx (and in test/harness.tsx) as well as the file's contents, and prove the assertion by deleting the import and watching it fail. Verified this dispatch: with the assertions added, deleting main.tsx's import fails 3 tests and deleting harness.tsx's fails 2; without them, zero.  
  <sub>IMP-0390 · `gate-cannot-fail`</sub>

The general rule the warning breaks: a check that identifies its target by subtracting known-innocent positions from all positions grows one exemption per shape forever and is wrong by construction on the shapes nobody has met yet; identify the claim positively (a declared field, or a single named position) instead. Third instance in this one predicate, after IMP-0196 and improvement review 19 change 7.  
  <sub>IMP-0328 · `gate-fires-on-nothing`</sub>
  <br><sub>**⚠ CONTESTED by `IMP-0557`** — a later finding disputes a claim in this lesson and NEITHER has been re-tested. Read that entry before relying on this one; it carries the form that is safe under either answer.</sub>
- Before wiring a new gate, run it against the WHOLE real corpus and read every finding, one by one, deciding true or false positive — the selftest proves the gate can fail, the corpus proves it fails on the right things, and these are different questions. Budget for it: three of four gates in one review were wrong on first contact with real data, and the most dangerous defect was not a false positive but a false NEGATIVE that a plausible matching rule produced (FIFO pairing of dispatches to terminal lines hid the one genuine stall while inventing a fake one). Where a gate reports 0 findings against a corpus you know contains an instance, that is the tell. State the measured precision in the review document — 'N findings across M documents, K true positives' — so the number is on the record rather than an impression.

  <sub>IMP-0315 · `hand-maintained-count-drifts-from-source`</sub>
- A new gate's selftest proves the gate against fixtures the gate's author wrote, which is the same person's model of the defect twice. Before believing a gate, run it against a REAL tree that contains the real defect -- `git archive HEAD <path> | tar -x -C <tmp>` reconstructs one in a line. A gate that cannot be shown failing over a genuine historical defect has not been shown to work at all, and for a gate over source in another language, the parser is the gate.  
  <sub>IMP-0282 · `gate-cannot-fail`</sub>
- A gate is not delivered when it is written and its selftest is green. It is delivered when a config names it. Writing the script and wiring it are one change, never two, and a review that writes a gate and defers the wiring has produced documentation. Where the gate is red against the real tree today, wire it SOFT with a --warn-only flag rather than deferring -- SOFT and visible beats HARD and absent.  
  <sub>IMP-0281 · `gate-cannot-fail`</sub>

Two things learned on the way: exclude the bare word 'deferred' from such cue lists, because 'IMP-0140 was deferred at the last review' is history rather than scope and suppressing on it would eat the real IMP-0154 claims; and a selftest case whose expectation is 'no warning' MUST assert the absence explicitly, since an exit-code-only assertion passes whether the warning appeared or not.

  <sub>IMP-0167 · `gate-cannot-fail`</sub>

  <sub>IMP-0159 · `gate-cannot-fail`</sub>

When adding check N to an existing multi-check gate, always add or extend the fixture AND the BuildGates.Tests.ps1 It block in the same change — do not assume the script's own docstring instructions substitute for a wired test. Fixed 2026-08-21: both fixtures completed (the label one needed an AppModules/AppModule.xml it was missing) and both wired in, plus three new fixtures for the checks added this session.  
  <sub>IMP-0141 · `gate-cannot-fail`</sub>
- When you change a <MaxLength> in Entity.xml, re-run every known-bad fixture that targets that column and confirm it still EXITS 1. A fixture padded to beat the old limit fits the new one, and the gate then passes on its own negative test - which reads as a broken gate, not as a fixture that needs relengthening. Widening 500 to 1000 turned src/tests/fixtures/known-bad/setting-description-length into a passing file on 2026-08-21. The general fix is to generate fixture padding from the declared limit rather than pinning it to a number.  
  <sub>IMP-0129 · `gate-cannot-fail`</sub>
- When a test protects an ordering guarantee, assert REACHABILITY, not a direct runAfter edge: walk the graph from the guarding action and require every other top-level action to be reachable from it. An edge assertion has to be loosened every time an action is inserted, and each loosening is a chance to weaken it by accident. Rewritten this way for FR-018 - it is now strictly stronger than the check it replaced.  
  <sub>IMP-0120 · `hand-maintained-count-drifts-from-source`</sub>

Use Get-DataverseWritePayload in src/tests/solutions/_harness/SolutionSource.psm1, which handles both, and assert the payload is NON-EMPTY before asserting anything about its contents. Note also that Get-FlowDefinition returns HASHTABLES: read keys with .Keys, never .PSObject.Properties, which on an IDictionary enumerates Count and IsReadOnly and silently finds nothing.

- rev_errorlog.rev_recordreference holds whatever the CALLING flow passed as text_3, which for the scoring flow is the application's rev_name (REV-2026-nnnn), not the submission id - only the intake flow's incomplete-payload path passes a TESTDATA- value. A cleanup filter must be written from what the writer writes, not from the marker the reader controls. And a deletion script that reports 0 has to be exercised against a non-empty table at least once, or 0 proves nothing.  
  <sub>IMP-0115 · `gate-cannot-fail`</sub>
- Before diagnosing why ONE flow's trigger does not fire, establish that ANY flow in that environment can run. A missing trigger registration and a dead flow runtime are indistinguishable from the record you are watching: both give no result and no error. Do not test three trigger configurations first, as this session did.  
  <sub>IMP-0107 · `two-invocation-paths-disagree`</sub>

  <sub>IMP-0077 · `two-invocation-paths-disagree`</sub>
- Scope a secret scan to what the build READS, never to `.`. Scanning build output means scanning tool-generated text with generic detectors, and the false positives land on a HARD gate. A gate that fires on nothing teaches people to ignore it — the mirror of a gate that cannot fire. When narrowing any security gate, add a test proving the narrowing did not remove the case it exists for.  
  <sub>IMP-0057 · `gate-fires-on-nothing`</sub>
- config/models.yml is the ONLY place a model id may appear, and it goes stale silently. Check it against the current Anthropic models page whenever a new Claude generation ships.   <sub>IMP-0053 · `two-invocation-paths-disagree`</sub>

Either read it from the document at run time, or assert the two are equal in a test. Check the DEFAULT of any parameter the build always overrides — it is the branch nothing exercises.  
  <sub>IMP-0051 · `two-invocation-paths-disagree`</sub>

A gate whose name matches no pattern in GATE_NAME_PATTERNS is silently exempt from the negative-test requirement — the gate-over-the-gates has a gate-shaped hole in it.

## Before you hand-author a platform artefact — capped lessons

*34 lesson(s) the digest does not render, in the same order it ranked them.*

- Every one of fifteen import failures was a plausible guess about a platform contract, committed to source, validated only by gates that could not detect it being wrong. Two failed guesses is the signal to stop guessing and go get ground truth.  
  <sub>IMP-0011 · `platform-contract-guessed-not-groundtruthed`</sub>
- rev_setting.rev_description is MaxLength=500. This project's verbose documentation style exceeds it. Same class as the flow 256-char cap.  
  <sub>IMP-0009 · `platform-field-length-limit-unenforced`</sub>
- An entity's FormXml/ and SavedQueries/ folders are dropped SILENTLY at pack time unless Entity.xml declares the empty <FormXml /> / <SavedQueries /> markers. 0 warnings, 0 errors, 0 components created.  
  <sub>IMP-0006 · `platform-contract-guessed-not-groundtruthed`</sub>
- Never infer a SolutionPackager file shape from documentation. Create the smallest real instance, export + unpack it, and copy the shape exactly.  
  <sub>IMP-0001 · `platform-contract-guessed-not-groundtruthed`</sub>
- An unfiltered/broadly-scoped `pac org fetch` against a high-volume system entity (importjob has entries going back to org creation, from every solution including Microsoft's own) can silently omit a live, matching row with no error or truncation notice -- verified 2026-09-03: importjob 2d9206a4-... existed and was absent from an unfiltered startedon-descending fetch but present the moment the same query added `solutionname eq 'RevitaliseGrantAutomation'` AND `startedon` = 'today'. Before concluding any live record 'does not exist' from a pac org fetch result, re-run the query narrowed by every filter available (name, date), never trust an absence from a broad/unfiltered fetch alone -- especially before writing an accusation of fabrication into an audit log.  
  <sub>IMP-0593 · `platform-contract-guessed-not-groundtruthed`</sub>
- Before writing 'known-broken' or 'trigger not registered' into a Deployment Summary based on a callbackregistration's createdon looking stale, run the definitive live test if the mechanism allows one: write the real trigger value and check whether the dependent record actually updates. A proxy signal (a timestamp) is not the same evidence as an observed effect, even when the proxy has correctly predicted failure before on a different flow.  
  <sub>IMP-0508 · `platform-contract-guessed-not-groundtruthed`</sub>
- When a business figure's SOURCE material shows a worked example (a real number, not just a label), check the new implementation's arithmetic against that example before treating a convention question as merely 'which of three plausible readings.' Round 3 and Round 4's near-identical 'Average 6 per day' despite very different cumulative totals (434 vs 717) was itself evidence the metric was cumulative-since-a-fixed-date, not per-round - available before ever asking the reviewer.  
  <sub>IMP-0507 · `platform-contract-guessed-not-groundtruthed`</sub>
- Microsoft's result() function is documented for Scope, For_each and Until only; whether it also resolves a Switch or If action's own name to the executed branch's top-level actions is UNCONFIRMED by any first-party page as of 2026-08-30. Any future use of this pattern on a Switch/If (not just this flow's two new call sites, carrying A-FLOW-13) must either cite this entry as the still-open assumption or ground-truth it live first - do not treat the existing REVIntakeWordPressToDataverse precedent as proof, since that one is confirmed only for a literal type:Scope.  
  <sub>IMP-0496 · `platform-fact-groundtruthed`</sub>
- XPath 1.0 sum() is 0 over an empty node set and NaN over a node set containing ANY empty element, and NaN is not valid JSON - so build the XML so an empty collection produces NO element at all: concat('<r>', if(empty(body('S')), '', concat('<v>', join(body('S'), '</v><v>'), '</v>')), '</r>'). join() over an empty array is '', which the surrounding element literals turn into the NaN case, so 'a presence filter removes the NaN case' is only true of blank values INSIDE a non-empty collection. And check where a NaN can escape to: a nested add() over per-group sums carries one group's NaN into a total, so a single empty group takes every metric in the document off the screen rather than one.  
  <sub>IMP-0473 · `platform-contract-guessed-not-groundtruthed`</sub>
- MemoAttributeMetadata.MaxLength's documented range (1 to 1048576) is not proof the upper bound actually works via a live CreateAttribute call -- it failed with a generic 0x80040216 on this environment. When a column's real content need is far below the documented ceiling (a JSON payload measured in KB, not MB), size it generously within this solution's own already-proven range (nothing here exceeds 4000 without a specific, working reason) rather than defaulting to 'as large as the platform allows' on the assumption that the documented maximum is a safe, tested value.  
  <sub>IMP-0367 · `platform-fact-groundtruthed`</sub>
- A binary asset imported from application code (not index.html/CSS) in a Vite-built Power Apps Code App should be inlined (`?inline` suffix) rather than left as a hashed, separately-emitted file with a runtime `import.meta.url` reference -- the latter is confirmed NOT to resolve correctly inside this Preview host, while index.html's own build-time-baked relative paths do. Apply this to any future binary asset this or other code apps in this solution bundle.  
  <sub>IMP-0362 · `platform-fact-groundtruthed`</sub>
- When a Code Apps connector symptom looks unfixable after checking identity/role/connection, the next cheapest step is reading Microsoft's own public sample for the SAME connector before escalating -- github.com/microsoft/PowerAppsCodeApps/samples/{Dataverse,DataverseConnector} are real, maintained, and directly comparable app structures, not documentation. IMP-0191's escalate-to-support conclusion is CORRECTED by this entry.  
  <sub>IMP-0360 · `platform-contract-guessed-not-groundtruthed`</sub>
- Before wiring a Code App to a Power Automate flow via `pa app add flow`, check the flow's own trigger kind first (`properties.definition.triggers.<name>.kind` in its workflow JSON) -- `PowerApp` (V1) is the legacy Canvas-App-only trigger and, on this project's evidence, its connections cannot be established or shared through any UI reachable for a Code App (no connector appears in the Connections gallery, no 'Run only users' tab applies). Recreate the trigger as `PowerAppV2` before attempting this integration again, and treat that as the untested precondition -- not yet proven to fix it, only identified as the one variable this project has not tried. Re-adding shared_logicflows without first resolving the trigger version would very likely reproduce the exact same boot failure.  
  <sub>IMP-0359 · `platform-fact-groundtruthed`</sub>
- Do not trust a `pa app add flow`-generated service's response TYPE as proof of what the flow returns -- check the flow's own Response actions (type Response, kind PowerApp) for a real statusCode/body before assuming a `void`-typed Run() means an empty response. src/dataverse/roundStatistics.ts's extractResponseText already reads the actual runtime value rather than the static type for exactly this reason and needs no change if the true behavior turns out to be a real JSON string despite the void type. The open half of A-LAND-2 (renamed, not reopened) is confirming which is true, and it needs a real trustee's session to observe.  
  <sub>IMP-0356 · `platform-fact-groundtruthed`</sub>
- A runAfter that lists Skipped FIRES when its predecessor is skipped - so an always-respond error branch is safe only in a flow with exactly ONE Response action. Before copying that wiring, count the Response actions in the target flow: in a multi-Response flow omit Skipped (the shape REVIntakeWordPressToDataverse's Respond_500_intake_failed already uses), or the error response also fires on every successful run, after the success response has already replied.  
  <sub>IMP-0345 · `platform-contract-guessed-not-groundtruthed`</sub>
- A code app reading a NEW Dataverse table needs `pa app add data-source --connector dataverse --table <t> -u <org-url> -c <connection-id>` as an explicit provisioning item, exactly as a new flow needs `pa app add flow`. Registering the entity set in client.ts's READ_SERVICES is not sufficient and cannot be: the SDK resolves a Dataverse-type data source from the generated dataSourcesInfo, so an unregistered table throws at runtime and at no earlier level.  
  <sub>IMP-0329 · `platform-contract-guessed-not-groundtruthed`</sub>
- A lookup column's properties come ONLY from $lookupBody inside ConvertTo-RevRelationshipBody, because ConvertTo-RevAttributeBody throws for Type 'lookup' — so every property a lookup will ever carry must be on that one hashtable. IsSecured was fixed there on 2026-08-24; IsAuditEnabled is still missing. It is one line of the same shape. Until it lands, do not set IsAuditEnabled=0 on any lookup column in Entity.xml and expect it to take effect: the column will be created with auditing on and no gate will fail, because the gate that knows about this records it as a declared KNOWN_GAP and warns rather than blocking.  
  <sub>IMP-0267 · `platform-contract-guessed-not-groundtruthed`</sub>
- A field permission in FieldSecurityProfiles.xml is only as real as the IsSecured flag on the attribute it names, and a relationship-created lookup column has no place in this project's current XML shape to carry that flag at all -- so nothing short of a live create call surfaces the gap (V3, not V1/V2). Before naming a lookup column in a field security profile, confirm the relationship or script path that creates it actually has a way to mark it secured; if it does not yet, that is schema work, not just a profile-membership edit.  
  <sub>IMP-0255 · `platform-contract-guessed-not-groundtruthed`</sub>
- A table's OwnershipType determines which privileges Dataverse will ever create for it: OrganizationOwned tables get no Assign/Share privilege at all, full stop. Before writing or copying a role's privilege block for a custom table, check that table's own OwnershipType first (rev_anonymisedstatistic in this same solution is the worked correct example). Separately: ensure-schema.ps1's "privilege does not exist" error message assumes exactly one cause (table not yet created) and should be broadened, since it produced a misleading remedy here.  
  <sub>IMP-0254 · `platform-contract-guessed-not-groundtruthed`</sub>
- Before replacing a compound-widget CHILD while keeping its Fluent PARENT, check whether the parent passes state through React context rather than through the DOM - grep the library for a `*Context` module and see which component consumes it. Fluent v9's RadioGroup publishes `name` and `checked` through RadioGroupContext and only Fluent's Radio reads it, so a look-alike child renders name=null on every input: single-selection, arrow-key traversal and the roving tabindex all come from the shared `name`, and losing them is a WCAG 1.3.1/2.1.1/4.1.2 regression that still looks correct on the first click. The same question applies to any Fluent group/child pair (Field, Accordion, Tablist, MenuList).  
  <sub>IMP-0388 · `platform-contract-guessed-not-groundtruthed`</sub>
- Never rely on `if()` (or any WDL conditional) to guard a division, an array index, or any other operation that throws on the untaken branch's own inputs -- both branches are evaluated regardless of the condition. Use a divisor-safe rewrite instead: `max(<divisor>,1)` as the denominator (never a literal 0) gives the same correct answer whenever the true divisor is 0, because the numerator is then necessarily 0 too. The shipped fix -- `mul(div(float(count),float(max(population,1))),100)` -- is now the pattern for every future percentage-over-a-possibly-zero-population computation in this project's flows.  
  <sub>IMP-0378 · `platform-fact-groundtruthed`</sub>
- Before assuming a generated file's escape-hatch workaround is merely a style choice, check whether the generated class ACTUALLY PARSES -- src/dataverse/README.md already documents this defect at file level (grepped, confirmed present), but no improvement-log entry existed naming the exact identifier or line. Worth reporting upstream (github.com/microsoft/PowerAppsCodeApps/issues) since it blocks every one of that class's 30+ typed methods, not just the one this app needs.  
  <sub>IMP-0361 · `platform-contract-guessed-not-groundtruthed`</sub>
- Filtering result(scope) for the child whose status is Failed only reaches the real failure when that scope's immediate children are all leaf actions. result() returns immediate children ONLY, so a Scope, Switch, If or Foreach among them collapses everything inside it into one wrapper result whose message is 'An action failed. No dependent actions succeeded.' Before copying this error-diagnosis pattern between flows, compare the two scopes' NESTING, not just their shape: recurse result() into the failed child when that child is itself a container.  
  <sub>IMP-0349 · `platform-contract-guessed-not-groundtruthed`</sub>
- A Power Apps code app calls a cloud flow with 'pa app add flow --flow-id <id>' -- solution-aware instant flows using the Power Apps trigger only, @microsoft/power-apps >= 1.1.1 -- which is a CLI-generated managed data source and therefore satisfies C-TECH-048. Do NOT use an HTTP-trigger URL or a custom API with MSAL for this: knowledge/technology/power-automate.md says to, and it is wrong and would violate a HARD constraint.  
  <sub>IMP-0304 · `platform-contract-guessed-not-groundtruthed`</sub>
- A constraint that forces a privileged identity to compute an aggregate says NOTHING about when it computes. Separate the two questions explicitly and justify staleness on its own merits, or you will ship a batch job and a table nobody asked for. On this stack the synchronous option is real and first-party: a Power Apps code app can call a solution-aware instant flow (Power Apps trigger only) with 'pa app add flow', so a privileged read can be live.  
  <sub>IMP-0303 · `platform-contract-guessed-not-groundtruthed`</sub>
- Before trying to fix a Code App's GENERIC (non-table) Dataverse connector data source's org-url-null symptom via CLI regeneration: (1) the new `pa` CLI's `app add data-source --connector dataverse` hard-requires --table in non-interactive mode, so it can never target the generic form at all; (2) the old `pac code add-data-source -env <org-url>` DOES run against the generic form, but grep the regenerated dataSourcesInfo.ts for the org URL string and for a non-empty tableId/version on the target block before believing anything was fixed -- a `dataSourceType: "Connector"` entry has no field to hold one, so a clean 'Data source added successfully' proves the schema was refreshed, not that org-url resolution changed. And when any `pac` command hangs past its documented duration with only a partial banner printed, check `pgrep -fl pac` for a stray long-lived `pac --non-interactive` process (including the one VS Code's own Power Platform extension bundles at .../microsoft-isvexptools.powerplatform-vscode/pac/pac, a DIFFERENT binary from ~/.dotnet/tools/pac) before concluding the command itself is broken -- this is the third command this stray-process class has been observed blocking (IMP-0215's `pac solution check`, IMP-0216's `pac org who`, now `pac code add-data-source`).  
  <sub>IMP-0226 · `platform-contract-guessed-not-groundtruthed`</sub>
- A hang that 'connects, then goes silent, with no correlation id' on macOS can have more than one simultaneous cause that produces the identical symptom: a stray process holding the MSAL token cache (IMP-0216) AND a stuck OS-level Keychain access permission prompt (a GUI dialog, invisible to any shell-based probe) are BOTH candidates, and fixing one does not rule out the other — test the fix by actually retrying the failing call, not by the plausibility of the mechanism alone. When `pac org who` or `pac solution check` hangs on a Mac with no output and no error, check Console.app / the user's screen for a pending Keychain access prompt (a modal dialog with no automated way to detect or dismiss it) in addition to `pgrep -fl pac`, and do not write a diagnosis into a knowledge file until the specific failing call has actually been re-run and observed to succeed.  
  <sub>IMP-0217 · `platform-contract-guessed-not-groundtruthed`</sub>
- Before framing one Power Platform tool as superseding another, check whether the vendor's own current agent-grounding files and template/plugin READMEs (not just Learn prose) already assume the replacement -- if they still instruct the 'superseded' tool, the migration is earlier/less complete than the prose suggests, and the doc should say so rather than presenting a clean handover.  
  <sub>IMP-0202 · `platform-contract-guessed-not-groundtruthed`</sub>
- Never infer that a service/automation account is the 'wrong' signed-in identity without asking first whether it is also the reviewer's own working credential for that specific customer engagement - some engagements provision exactly one shared account, interactive and non-interactive uses included. Ask 'is this your own account for this customer, or a different one?' before diagnosing an identity mismatch, rather than assuming standard service-account/human-account separation holds.  
  <sub>IMP-0190 · `platform-contract-guessed-not-groundtruthed`</sub>
- A Power Apps Code App's power.config.json connectionReferences entry is a LOCAL manifest key naming the connector it needs - it carries no connectionId and does not correspond to any Dataverse connectionreference table row (confirmed by querying every connectionreference row in the org and finding none matching). The connection is resolved per-signed-in-user at runtime by the host, so a maker deleting/recreating THEIR OWN Connection in make.powerapps.com never touches a different user's binding - when "Invalid organization URL 'null' provided" appears for one specific user, check whether THAT user (not the maker) has ever created a Microsoft Dataverse connection at make.powerapps.com/connections themselves before re-suspecting the app's shared connection or any connection reference. Also: `pac env fetch -xf <file>` runs an arbitrary read-only FetchXML query against Dataverse under the CURRENTLY SELECTED pac auth profile - no PROVISION_APP_ID/certificate needed - and is the way to get a solution's real solutionid (pac solution list never shows it) or query any table directly when the cert-based provisioning identity's credentials are not loaded in the current shell.

- pac code ground truth (pac 2.4.1, verified 2026-08-21): `pac code init` creates ONLY power.config.json - it does not scaffold React, so the Vite project is hand-authored; `pac code add-data-source` generates the GENERIC Dataverse connector typing with no per-table models (grep -c rev_ returns 0); `pac code list-tables`/`list-datasets` fail with an empty `{}` against this connection on all three dataset forms, so the typed route is unreachable here; and the generated MicrosoftDataverseService.ts DOES NOT COMPILE - a parameter named `MSCRM.IncludeMipSensitivityLabel` contains an illegal `.`. A bare `&pagetype=...` fragment is not a URL; the app designer rejects it with 'expects a web resource' and the sub-area disappears from play mode. Read the shape off a Microsoft-authored managed sitemap in the same org — 'Power Platform Environment Settings' has 25 examples — rather than inferring it. AND NOTE: a leading-slash URL carries no host, so it is environment-independent and does NOT breach C-TECH-047; the solution-awareness objection to hardcoding a URL is answered by the relative form, not by avoiding URLs.

Do NOT fix it with a second guess — that is what produced the first one. Use the A-001 method that worked: have the reviewer point ONE sub-area at the intended view in the app designer, save and publish, then read the platform's own regenerated sitemapxml back via the Web API and copy that exact shape for the rest. ## Before you declare a deploy or an import successful — capped lessons

*5 lesson(s) the digest does not render, in the same order it ranked them.*

- statecode=0 on a cloud flow means DRAFT, not activated, and a solution import never turns a flow on. Query workflows(<id>)?$select=statecode and read 1 as Activated; do not accept a Deployment Summary's word for it - this project's own summary labelled statecode=0 'activated' while its Dev Summary correctly called the same value Draft. A flow in Draft receives no trigger, so a row created against it is never processed and never will be.  
  <sub>IMP-0100 · `v3-does-not-imply-v4`</sub>
- Renders-in-edit-mode is not renders-in-play-mode. A site map confirmed by Web API query, in a published app, can still fail to render for a user — so V4 stays a named human step and is never inferred from a successful query, however thorough. When it happens, re-check after propagation time before diagnosing, and check the sub-area shape (IMP-0087) before blaming the platform.  
  <sub>IMP-0088 · `v3-does-not-imply-v4`</sub>
- A manifest's source_commit only describes the artifact if the working tree was clean when the pack ran. Record `git status --porcelain` alongside the sha and state the count, because a sha copied from HEAD over a dirty tree names source the zip does not contain — build #7's manifest named a commit predating the whole rev_grant table it had just packaged.  
  <sub>IMP-0078 · `exit-zero-does-not-mean-created`</sub>
- Invoiced hours are not completed hours. Never compute a variance against an estimate for a phase still in progress: the phase looks efficient right up until the remaining work is booked. Before comparing actuals to an estimate, establish that the phase is CLOSED - client testing and feedback included, since those are the activities most likely to be outstanding when the build looks done.  
  <sub>IMP-0065 · `exit-zero-does-not-mean-created`</sub>
- Solution import RELABELS matching option values but does NOT delete values the new source omits. Orphaned values survive every subsequent import. Compare live option-set members against source.  
  <sub>IMP-0019 · `exit-zero-does-not-mean-created`</sub>


## Before you report SUCCESS at all — capped lessons

*29 lesson(s) the digest does not render, in the same order it ranked them.*

- A build manifest's free-text provenance note is an unchecked claim about shipped content - resolve every artefact it names to a path on disk before trusting it, because no gate reads that prose. Record the dirty-path COUNT (IMP-0078) and stop there; enumerating what the dirty tree contains restates the dispatch's intended scope, not the tree's actual contents.  
  <sub>IMP-0324 · `no-assertion-on-shipped-content`</sub>
- Stamp `reviewed_in` on every finding a review processes WHEN THE DRAFT IS WRITTEN, not when the keyword arrives — that stamp is the only thing that makes the entry read as `awaiting-approval` ('read the document, send the keyword') instead of `unread` ('nobody has looked'). Status moves to APPLIED on approval; the stamp goes on at draft time. agents/improvement-agent.md step 8 currently describes only the approval-time half, which is why review 41 left a fully-analysed blocker reading as unread and re-summoned a strategic-tier session.  
  <sub>IMP-0488 · `learning-substrate-destroyed`</sub>
- A review that APPENDS its own findings must set `appended_by` and NOT `reviewed_in`. Setting both makes the entry read as `awaiting-approval`, which tells every later review to send a keyword against a document that never mentions it — a state no session can clear, and the queue reads as handled. The fix is always to DROP the false `reviewed_in` and keep `appended_by`; never to move the stamp forward, which is what the gate's own message used to advise. scripts/verify-improvement-log.py now fails on this via check_self_stamps(). And the general shape, which is the more valuable half: when a gate's finding is real but its printed REMEDY is wrong, the remedy is part of the defect — measured 31 findings unnarrowed (26 historical entries with no `appended_by`, which would have made the gate permanently red), narrowed to 6 findings / 6 true / 0 false with 9 true negatives.  
  <sub>IMP-0456 · `learning-substrate-destroyed`</sub>
- When an ADR moves columns off a table but retains them, sweep the artefacts that describe the TABLE, not only the ones that write or read the columns: the entity-level <Description>, the global option set's <Description>, and the flow's notes. On rev_roundstatisticsrequest all three still said the flow writes the answer there three days after ADR-038, inside the same file whose attribute descriptions now carry 'Written by nothing and read by nothing' — a shipped artefact contradicting itself eight lines apart. The mechanical form is one grep per moved column against Entities/*/Entity.xml entity-level descriptions and OptionSets/*.xml, and it is the natural second half of verify-superseded-column-writers.py. And never cite a shipped <Description> as saying something without grepping the description: TAD section 3.9.2 claimed this option set's description recorded the naming mismatch, and it did not.  
  <sub>IMP-0448 · `no-assertion-on-shipped-content`</sub>
- Before designing a gate, grep docs/improvements/ for an unapproved review proposing it - a parked review is invisible to the queue gate AND to every other dispatch, so 'no finding says this is being fixed' is not evidence that nobody is fixing it. Review 36 and IMP-0436 designed the same provisioning-coverage gate within the hour; the shipped file records the alternative filename in its docstring so a grep for either finds it, which is the mitigation available after the fact rather than before. Two corollaries measured in the same interval, both worth internalising: a line citation written into a review document can rot before the keyword arrives (three did, in the review's own Summary), so re-grep every cited line number at application; and a measurement can move under you - this one went from 6 findings to 3 - so re-run every number the gate output states rather than trusting the draft.  
  <sub>IMP-0443 · `learning-substrate-destroyed`</sub>
- When an ADR retains superseded columns instead of deleting them, check BOTH directions before writing 'written by nothing and read by nothing' into shipped metadata: grep provisioning/ and Workflows/ for the old entity set name paired with the column (a retained column is a live write target), and grep the app's own column list for the read half. rev_status on rev_roundstatisticsrequest is written by seed-round-statistics-request.ps1 line 105 and read by nothing, so its <Description> is false in one direction and that script's own header rationale is false in the other. Deciding which artefact changes is delivery work, not a documentation tidy-up: dropping the write leaves the retained column genuinely dead, correcting the wording keeps a deliberate default in place.  
  <sub>IMP-0438 · `no-assertion-on-shipped-content`</sub>
  <br><sub>**⚠ CORRECTED by `IMP-0446`** — a later finding contradicts this lesson. Read both before acting on it; the marker does not decide which is right.</sub>
- A test harness must compose the same providers and the same theme object the composition root composes, or every rendering test asserts markup the app never produces. When a bootstrap file is excluded from coverage, check what it is the ONLY importer of — that is the code nothing measures. A file at 0% coverage inside an aggregate threshold is silent.  
  <sub>IMP-0353 · `no-assertion-on-shipped-content`</sub>
- A build manifest field that no gate asserts can vanish between two consecutive builds of the same feature with every gate green. Before citing a manifest field as evidence, check whether anything requires it; and for the wbs field specifically, assert its presence and that every id resolves against contract/wbs.json, because that field is the join key between a commit, a contract line and an invoice.  
  <sub>IMP-0350 · `no-assertion-on-shipped-content`</sub>
- When you amend an improvement review that is already parked at its gate, reconcile the gate block FIRST and write the amendment note LAST. The note is a claim about work, so producing it before the work means an interruption leaves a false completion claim instead of a to-do list. The incremental rule step 8 states for applying a review applies unchanged to amending a draft.  
  <sub>IMP-0333 · `learning-substrate-destroyed`</sub>
- A generated artefact carries no staleness signal at its point of use, so an agent reading .claude/agents/<name>.md cannot tell that the generator has moved on — which makes 'the files were regenerated' a claim that must be measured, never inherited. Run generate-subagents.py --check yourself before writing that the 18 files are current; two artefacts asserted it in the 26 hours the files were actually stale, and one of them was an APPLIED entry's own evidence. When a review's apply step is interrupted, every claim in its document about work after the interruption point is unverified by construction (IMP-0301) — and the next session's verification table is exactly where those claims get laundered into fact.  
  <sub>IMP-0309 · `learning-substrate-destroyed`</sub>
- Do the bookkeeping incrementally, not as a final step: mark each finding APPLIED as its change lands, so an interrupted improvement review leaves a truthful log instead of a tree that disagrees with it. Six of review 27's twelve changes sat on disk for four hours while all ten of its findings still read NEW and the gate demanded a review of work already half done — IMP-0033's lesson exactly, one level up: an unreconciled log cannot tell 'nothing was learned' from 'nobody did the bookkeeping'. When resuming an interrupted apply, verify each change against disk before redoing it, and never trust the review document's own status header (IMP-0204).  
  <sub>IMP-0301 · `learning-substrate-destroyed`</sub>
- An entry whose proposed_change names several targets is not closed by shipping the cheapest one. Before marking APPLIED, split proposed_change.target on '+' and ',' and account for EVERY path - either it changed, or applied_by says which part was deliberately not done and why. The cheapest deliverable is usually the knowledge line and the expensive one is usually the gate, so closing on a subset systematically drops exactly the mechanical half this system says is the only half that works.  
  <sub>IMP-0251 · `learning-substrate-destroyed`</sub>
- When two proposed changes touch the SAME section of the same file and only one is approved, apply the approved one as a minimal edit, never as a whole-section rewrite - a rewrite carries the withheld text in with it and the review's own change table will still say it was withheld. And when a review parks a decision, re-read the target lines after applying everything else and before writing the 'what you need to decide' section: a decision the reviewer is asked to make about text that is already in force is not a decision. Fourth generation of one substrate defect: IMP-0154 a REVIEW leaving no trace, IMP-0169 a DELIVERY FIX leaving no trace, IMP-0181 an APPROVAL leaving no trace, this one a WITHHOLDING leaving no trace.  
  <sub>IMP-0250 · `learning-substrate-destroyed`</sub>
- A review document's status HEADER and its Applied SECTION can contradict each other, and the header is the one that is stale -- Review 10 said 'nothing has been applied' above a section 9 recording the approval and four items that were on disk. Never read a review's disposition from its header: check whether it has an 'Applied' section, then verify that section's claims against the working tree (IMP-0181 said verify a review's proposals against the tree and never against its prose; this is the same defect one level up, in the status line itself).   <sub>IMP-0204 · `learning-substrate-destroyed`</sub>
- An evidence_grep needle that is ABSENT is as informative as one that is present, and nothing reads it that way: the log gate checks needles for APPLIED entries and for the already-fixed state only, so four items of APPROVED, unapplied work read as 'accepted reviewed deferrals'. Third generation of one substrate defect in three days - IMP-0154 is a REVIEW leaving no trace, IMP-0169 a DELIVERY FIX leaving no trace, this one an APPROVAL leaving no trace. Two consequences worth remembering independently of the fix: a review document's own status header is a CLAIM (review 6 says nothing was applied; 9 of 12 items were), so verify a review's proposals against the working tree and never against its prose; and only 26 of 164 APPLIED entries carry a needle at all, so the requirement has to bind going forward rather than retroactively or it reports 138 errors about work that is done.  
  <sub>IMP-0181 · `learning-substrate-destroyed`</sub>
- Before treating a NEW finding as live work, check whether its fix already shipped — IMP-0155 summoned a strategic-tier review as an unread blocker while the generalisation it demanded was already committed in the same tree, visible in EnsureSchema.Tests.ps1's own comment naming IMP-0155 by id.   <sub>IMP-0169 · `learning-substrate-destroyed`</sub>
- Before re-deriving a blocker's analysis, grep docs/improvements/ for its IMP id — a review may already have processed it and stalled at its gate, and the log gate cannot tell that from an unread entry. When a review processes an entry, stamp reviewed_in on EVERY entry it processed, not only the ones it defers: review 4 stamped IMP-0149 and not IMP-0148, and the missing stamp cost a duplicated strategic-tier dispatch five hours later. ## Capabilities established in earlier sessions — capped lessons

*44 lesson(s) the digest does not render, in the same order it ranked them.*

- Dataverse column-level WRITE control exists and is already used in this solution: FieldPermission carries CanRead, CanUpdate and CanCreate (Other/FieldSecurityProfiles.xml:112-114) and ensure-schema.ps1 writes all three. It is unusable for a column a CODE APP must read, for two project-specific reasons and not a platform one -- CanUpdate governs only IsSecured=1 columns; releasing a secured column to a trustee needs the trustee team inside a field security profile, which no-trustee-in-column-security-profile forbids and which is ADR-002's whole control; and a secured column on a table the app queries fails no-secured-columns-in-code-app. Never write 'the platform cannot' where 'our own HARD gates forbid' is the true statement: the design is the same and the sentence is not.  
  <sub>IMP-0403 · `platform-fact-groundtruthed`</sub>
- To read a field security profile's column membership live: filter by the PROFILE's name through a link-entity and compare client-side - never put a condition on fieldpermission.entityname, which raises a System.Int32 FormatException exactly as systemform.objecttypecode does. The working query is a fetch over fieldpermission selecting attributelogicalname and entityname, link-entity to fieldsecurityprofile on fieldsecurityprofileid with a name-eq condition. Generalise the rule: on Dataverse metadata tables an EntityName-typed column can be SELECTED but not FILTERED as a string. Also: the FetchXML 'attribute' entity carries logicalname but not issecured, so column-security flags must come from the Web API metadata path, not FetchXML.  
  <sub>IMP-0373 · `platform-fact-groundtruthed`</sub>
- A background Agent-tool dispatch cannot resume itself from a Monitor or background-task notification it creates -- only the dispatching session receives those. If a dispatch's final message describes work as pending on 'I'll resume automatically when X completes,' treat that exactly like a spend-limit death: the dispatch has actually stopped, X will never be acted on by that agent, and the dispatcher must verify live state directly and do the smallest remaining reconciliation itself rather than waiting for a resumption that is not coming. A 'completed' task-notification status describes only that the agent's own turn ended with no live children -- it does not mean the agent's stated goal was reached.  
  <sub>IMP-0357 · `dispatched-agent-stalls-silently`</sub>
- Never bundle a font file that arrived with a brand handover without checking its web-embedding licence separately from the desktop one — an Office/Microsoft 365 font (Aptos, and the same applies to Segoe UI) is licensed for device install and document embedding, not for a site to serve. The compliant, zero-cost implementation is name-only in the CSS font stack with a full system fallback chain: the viewer's own installed copy is used where present, and nothing is served. Record the substitution rather than making it silently, because the rendered result differs per device.

Both facts are E2 (vendor documentation), not yet observed live on this project.

- A Power Apps Code App cannot aggregate: the generated IGetAllOptions has no 'apply' member, so no server-side $apply/groupby reaches the typed services, and the app runs as the signed-in user so column security nulls every secured column a tally would need.   <sub>IMP-0278 · `change-order-sizing-without-precedent`</sub>
- Reading Dataverse relationship metadata: RelationshipDefinitions(SchemaName='x') alternate-key addressing WORKS (confirmed live 2026-08-24, closing the caveat in ensure-schema.ps1's own header), but NEVER put CascadeConfiguration in $select — it is a complex property and the answer is a bare HTTP 400 with no property named, which reads exactly like the relationship being absent. Omit $select and read it off the full response. Two sibling limits on the same endpoints: startswith() is unsupported on Metadata Entities entirely (0x8006088a — filter by exact equality, or address by alternate key), and Privileges is NOT an expandable navigation property on EntityMetadata (0x80060888 — use the `privileges` entity set). More generally, on metadata endpoints a 400 usually means your PROJECTION is illegal, not that the thing is missing: retry without $select before concluding absence.  
  <sub>IMP-0261 · `platform-fact-groundtruthed`</sub>
- A Dataverse lookup column IS fully securable (CanBeSecuredForRead=True, verified live 2026-08-24) — never treat a failing field permission on a lookup as a platform limit the way a primary name genuinely is. BUT securing a lookup hides only the GUID: the <lookup>name companion column beside it carries the related row's primary name VALUE and reports CanBeSecuredForRead=False, exactly like a Money _base twin. So before securing a lookup for confidentiality, ask what the TARGET table's primary name actually contains. In this solution rev_applicant/rev_grant/rev_bankaccount all have autonumber or masked primary names, so their companions leak only a pseudonymous reference — but rev_provideridname leaks the provider's real organisation name, and the only control on it is the table privilege (NFR-002: Finance-only Read). Read securability with: EntityDefinitions(LogicalName='<t>')/Attributes?$select=LogicalName,AttributeType,IsSecured,CanBeSecuredForRead,CanBeSecuredForCreate,CanBeSecuredForUpdate.  
  <sub>IMP-0257 · `platform-fact-groundtruthed`</sub>
- An OrganizationOwned Dataverse table exposes exactly six privileges — Create, Read, Write, Delete, Append, AppendTo — and NO Assign and NO Share, ever, because there is no individual owner to assign to or share from. DELETE DOES EXIST; the missing set is exactly {Assign, Share}, and conflating the two is what makes this easy to get wrong (rev_anonymisedstatistic withholds Delete as a deliberate policy choice, not a platform limit). Verified live across all four OrganizationOwned and all six UserOwned tables in DEV, 2026-08-24. Read it for any table with: privileges?$filter=endswith(name,'<table>')&$select=name — that lists exactly what the environment will accept, and EntityDefinitions(LogicalName='<t>')?$select=OwnershipType says which set to expect. Note Privileges is NOT an expandable navigation property on EntityMetadata (0x80060888), so query the `privileges` entity set, not $expand.

## Unrouted — no section assigned — capped lessons

*229 lesson(s) the digest does not render, in the same order it ranked them.*

- Before designing to an approved requirement that says an app should READ a column, check whether that column is in a field security profile AND whether a build gate forbids referencing it - no-secured-columns-in-code-app fails on any secured column the Code App names, whatever the intent. And never accept 'column security will withhold it' as a safety argument without naming EVERY persona that opens the surface: this app is read by the process owner as well as by trustees, and she IS a profile member, so the same query returns real values for her. FR-078's 'restricted' state must therefore be RENDERED from a build-derived field catalogue, never inferred from a null a query returned.

## Rendered lessons the digest truncated, in full

*64 lesson(s) the digest shows in shortened form. Each is cut at a sentence boundary once it exceeds 600 characters and marked `[…]` there; this is the complete text.*

- When a freshness/staleness bound is deliberately allowed to be unset as a fail-safe default, trace its effect through EVERY code path that uses the same comparison, not just the primary one it was designed for. Here, a bound meant to prevent 'skip recomputation and show something stale' also silently defeated 'accept the recomputation I just triggered and watched finish' -- because both checks shared one expression. Either seed a real value for RoundStatisticsStaleAfterSeconds now, or (durable fix) give fetchRoundStatistics's poll loop its own acceptance test -- a document whose computedOn is strictly after the moment this cycle wrote rev_triggeredon is current, independent of staleAfterSeconds -- rather than reusing isCurrent() for both purposes.  
  <sub>IMP-0511 · `gate-cannot-fail`</sub>
- When a flow's answer moves from an HTTP response into a Dataverse row, re-derive WHO CAN WRITE that row before anything else: the app needs Write on the table to place its request, and one table serving both directions of the exchange hands the caller Write over the answer too. Split request and result into two tables so the boundary is a table privilege -- column-level write control (FieldPermission CanUpdate) exists but governs only IsSecured=1 columns, and securing a column the app must read both fails no-secured-columns-in-code-app and needs a profile membership no-trustee-in-column-security-profile forbids. Then check IsAuditEnabled on the answer column: an overwritable aggregate with auditing off is unattributable, and every column gate in this repository is read-side, so none of them will tell you.  
  <sub>IMP-0401 · `gate-scope-mismatch`</sub>
- Before believing a fix to a provisioning script's payload-building function is complete, check whether the step that CALLS it is create-only. ensure-schema.ps1's relationship step reports EXISTS and skips, so a corrected relationship/lookup body never reaches an environment where the relationship already exists — the fix lands in a fresh PRD and never in DEV, which is the harder direction to notice because DEV is where testing happens. A create-only step needs a paired reconcile step for every property that can be corrected in source later (step 3b is that step for lookup IsSecured, one-directional by design: unsecured to secured only, never the reverse, because removing a column-level control is a human decision). And when testing an idempotent script, the state that matters is not 'everything absent' or 'everything present' but PRESENT-BUT-WRONG — the only one of the three that a partial live run actually leaves behind.  
  <sub>IMP-0259 · `two-invocation-paths-disagree`</sub>
- A compound deliverable ('X + access test') needs its evidence rule split so the human-verification half is tracked separately from the buildable half, and left permanently unsatisfiable by repository evidence alone -- report it as derived_status=partial (or a new manual_verification_required state) until a dated V4 confirmation exists, never as complete. This is the third time 6.5 specifically has produced a false-complete reading (after the original 8.2/6.5 forward-reference pair, IMP-0067); per skills/how-to-promote-a-finding.md two instances of one class demand generalisation, and this is the second recorded instance for the SAME task id, which is stronger evidence still.  
  <sub>IMP-0230 · `gate-cannot-fail`</sub>
- verify-design-doc-claims.py's retraction blind spot (IMP-0428) is not a one-time cost paid once per document — it recurs every time a NEW sentence explains or cross-references an already-retracted claim, even in a document review 36 already made green. Author guidance embedded only in the gate's failure message does not reach the author before the sentence is written. Before adding prose that names a corrected rev_* absence claim (for cross-reference, erratum-convention explanation, or any other reason), grep the target script's own FAILED-message text for its authoring rule first, or route the cross-reference through the section number alone ("see Section 3.4's correction") with no column name and no quoted absence phrase in the same sentence.  
  <sub>IMP-0535 · `gate-fires-on-nothing`</sub>
- A gate that CRASHES has not failed safe - it has stopped being a gate, and every rule that says 'run the validator first' silently becomes unenforced. Two concrete fixes, both cheap: (1) validate `proposed_change` is a dict in the schema check, so a malformed entry is reported by ID at the point the log is read rather than surfacing later as a traceback; (2) make every consumer type-guard rather than None-guard - `isinstance(row.get('proposed_change'), dict)`, not `or {}`. And the general shape: a latent malformation can be unreachable until a STATUS CHANGE makes a code path execute over it, so the session that trips a crash is often not the session that caused it - check `git diff` on the data before assuming your own change broke the checker. The immediate unblock is to fix IMP-0390's and IMP-0391's `proposed_change` into objects; the durable fix is the type guard. AND: a type guard stops the crash without fixing the data - guarding the consumer and validating the schema are two different jobs, and doing only the first converts a loud failure into a silent one.

Check with: environmentvariabledefinitions?$select=schemaname,defaultvalue&$expand=environmentvariabledefinition_environmentvariablevalue($select=value) - if the value comes from defaultvalue, it will not survive the next deploy. seed-test-data.ps1 now reports the source of each value and blocks when rev_ProcessOwnerUpn is empty.  
  <sub>IMP-0121 · `v3-does-not-imply-v4`</sub>
- A callbackregistration row surviving a solution import is not evidence that the trigger works. Compare its createdon against the flow's modifiedon: if the registration predates the import, it pins logicappsversion to a definition version that no longer exists, and Dataverse delivers events into nothing - no run, no error, empty run history. Existence is the wrong assertion. The registration must be RECREATED: turn the flow off, confirm the row disappears, then turn it on from the DESIGNER and confirm a row with a NEW createdon appears. Deploying a Dataverse-triggered flow therefore has a mandatory post-deploy step that no import performs and no query can substitute for.

If neither fires and callbackregistrations is 0, every remaining cause is OUTSIDE Dataverse (connection health, DLP policy, a subscription error shown only in the maker UI) and no amount of further querying will find it: hand it to someone with the Power Automate UI. Also: a designer save can silently change the trigger's scope (4 Organization -> 1 User here), so re-read subscriptionRequest/scope out of workflow.clientdata after any save and compare it against solution source. Two Web API details found on the way: ownerid expands to the 'principal' type which has NO fullname (select _ownerid_value and resolve it separately), and Write-Output inside a PowerShell function merges into that function's return value - use Write-Host for progress lines.

Fix it by opening the flow in the Power Automate DESIGNER and saving it, not by toggling it in the Solutions list.
